ثَلِبٌ : see ثِلْبٌ. ―
-b2- Also, applied to a spear, (S, M, A, K, but in a copy of the A written ↓ ثِلْبٌ ,) Much notched, or broken in the edges
[of the head]: (S, M, K:) or weak, or weak and soft. (A.) You say ثِلْبٌ عَلَى ثِلْبٍ وَبِيَدِهِ ثَلِبٌ [An extremely old, or old and weak, man, whose teeth are much broken, upon a camel in the like condition, and having in his hand a spear that is much notched, or weak, or weak and soft]. (A, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
